subject.title: fix(sessions): enforce exact owner equality for all parent session use

question: Should plugin-runtime access to legacy ownerless parent and existing-target session rows fail closed immediately, or must this PR provide an explicit migration or compatibility window?
rationale: Exact owner equality closes the confidentiality gap, but ownerless historical rows cannot be safely attributed and rejecting them may stop existing plugin workflows; repository policy requires maintainers to own this security-versus-upgrade boundary.

options.title: Fail closed now
options.body: Reject ownerless rows for plugin-runtime callers, document the upgrade impact in the PR, add cross-store proof, and merge once checks pass.

options.title: Add migration first
options.body: Provide a narrowly justified doctor or migration path that can safely establish ownership before enforcing exact equality.

options.title: Preserve ownerless compatibility
options.body: Allow legacy ownerless rows temporarily, accepting that plugin identity cannot be proven and the reported isolation boundary remains weaker.

recommendation.title: Fail closed now
recommendation.body: Reject ownerless rows for plugin-runtime callers, document the upgrade impact in the PR, add cross-store proof, and merge once checks pass.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work most directly owns session ownership metadata and its propagation through gateway session flows.
